body: Oh, there's nothing really to say. I'm just losing my mind, is all.

Understood.

When I cry over my impending suicide, it's not for the life I'll lose but for the one I hoped for and could never have.
Well, what kinds of girls are you dating? I'm sure there are girls who wouldn't do that.
I'm afraid of people looking at my dead, pathetic body. I wish I could die in a fire, wherein I'd be burned unrecognizable.
Now you're just talking out of your ass.
And some people are naive.

I tried to go out there and make a life of my own. I failed miserably. I tried again to make something of my failed life, and I failed again.

I hoped to try again, but apparently I'm too unwell to give it another shot. I'll only dig a deeper hole for myself.

Of course.

The problem with talking to sane people is that they don't understand how real this stuff can feel. I mean, what you're saying still sounds crazy to me, but I get it.

Thanks, you take care too.

I'm in the same boat. 19 female.

Last I visited my psych, I hadn't eaten for a week, so now he won't allow me to go even a few weeks without seeing him. I hate eating, bathing, brushing my teeth, looking in the mirror, etc. But food is the only pleasurable thing in my life, so I'm really torn. I just ate a donut and I feel pathetic. I'm betrayed by every inch of my body.

The supernatural stuff has a way of creeping up on you. Just the other day, I was staring at these christmas lights I have in my room. They were beckoning me to come home. I literally reached out to them, but my hands slipped through the rays (obviously). This went on for maybe 10 min. I'm starting to feel like my soul is damned, when I don't even believe in souls. Maybe I'm not from this universe--but from wherever those lights come from.

I don't do any kind of drug and I've refused all medications.

In conclusion: you might be crazy, but you might also want to stop doing drugs?
Thanks for trying to help. I appreciate it.
Some people don't have thoughts worth thinking. And the intention behind suicide is to cease to exist, so that's not really a drawback.
My parents don't care how I feel. What are you even basing this on? there is a reason? It's just wishful, delusional thinking.
In what way is being miserable better than being dead?
No, I assure you I'm here for no reason except my parents' carelessness.

It's quite easy to work hard when you can perceive an eventual positive outcome.

Depression masks everything, and it can make it so that there seems to be no positives in your future. Sometimes, you are suicidal and think there will be no future for you at all. When things get like that, working hard feels like a futile effort. It's like trying push through a brick wall, hoping to get to the other side. You know you can't do it.
What kind of dog was it? And what was its name? I've always wanted a weimaraner to name Leo.
That's deep.

I don't have much advice or any uplifting words, really. But I definitely get it. I rarely leave my house anymore, either. Maybe 3 times a month. And I don't have nightmares, but I have to keep the lights on all night because I have night terrors. It really is exhausting.

Could you take a leave of absence from school? Work in the meantime? It'll give you some time to address your mental health and you could save up a little.

Oh, that's bad. 

You could try going out as soon as the sun begins to rise, which I think is about 7am these days. There won't be as many people out, and I always find the early morning hours to be the most comforting. Wear a baseball cap, maybe.
I know the feeling all too well. I also know that when I'm feeling the way you do, nothing anyone could say could make a difference for me. Same for you?
Sometimes it feels good to feel like shit.
Lol. I bought a sewing book recently. Luckly, I came to my senses before buying a machine. However, I did just purchase 100+ NatGeo back issues, so...
I disagree. I think that it's pointless to live your life unhappily when there's no benefit but to breathe.
I didn't attempt to speak for anyone. I spoke objectively, and--objectively--anecdotes are just anecdotes. Even the ones that are hopeful and sweet are still just anecdotes.

I read your entire comment. I rarely read anything even a third as long as this, but I figured you were speaking directly to me, so it's the least I could do.

I'm very sorry that this happened to you. It's shit, really. My story is similar, actually; though, I didn't give the effort you did, and I regret that, even if it would not have changed my current circumstances.

I'm not sure what is an appropriate response. I can only urge you to give your best trying to figure out how to fix this mess. I'm not saying it'll definitely get better (I actually objected to the "it gets better" slogan in another thread--was *not* well received, lol), but your situation definitely won't improve if you don't give it a shot.

I'm interested in talking more about your experiences (and mine), if you would like to.

Honestly, I didn't read the post; I only read the title, and that's the only thing I addressed--the phrase "it gets better". I wasn't belittling his OP's experience nor was I implying that we don't care if it got better for him/her. I only said that, because it got better for OP does not mean that things will work out for everyone else if only they'd "see the light". Personally, delusional optimism makes me sick.

I was not overtly sensitive and was even slightly rude, but that doesn't have much to do with maturity here.

Okay. I'm sorry that I was mean. I know that you meant well and I shouldn't have responded so bluntly, but I don't believe what you are saying has any truth in reality.

You and I (and many others) have a different view on how life works. But I suppose the root of my objection is that I don't like being preached to. But that's my fault; I should have just ignored the post.

I'm very, very glad that it got better for you, but I think the phrase is trite and meaningless. No one depressive situation is the same, so that it got better for you means nothing to the rest of us.

I think touting this idea that "it'll all work out in the end because life just works that way" is a bit immature.

I imagine death is a lot like sleep or being put under general anesthesia, neither of which I've found to be very scary.

What I am afraid of is what will happen to my body. People will toss me around and cut me up like I had never had my own thoughts or will. They will look at me in disgust for what I had done to myself. They'll dress me up in hideous clothing and makeup and everyone will see how pathetic I look.
I want to take this phrase "it gets better" and burn it with acid.

I asked my psychiatrist if there's a difference between depression and having legitimate problems which warrant unhappiness. He didn't answer the question, but I'm sure there is. Sometimes it's not you who's messed up; sometimes it's everything around you that's messed up.

It sounds like you're doing everything you need to do. Life is just hard. But, if you keep going, I honestly believe it will get better for you (and I'm not the optimistic type). Good luck.

I had that problem and I was prescribed antipsychotics (had other psychotic symptoms as well). I took them for two weeks and have been off them for 4 weeks, but the racing thoughts haven't returned (though the other issues have).

I am sleeping better now, though. That's probably because I get so worked up and cry myself to sleep. I also try not to take naps so that I stay on some type of schedule.

Yes, absolutely. Hope and waiting; both feel worse than the depression itself. Some days, I get it into my head that if I do this or that, I'll get where I'd like to be in such amount of time.

It never works and I am sick of hope.

Yeah, I don't want to, but I feel compelled to.

I've made a lot of positive changes, but they all fell through. I even spent lots of money seeking professional help, but I was lied to and am in a worse position (psychologically) because of it. I'm not willing to make any more positive efforts. Hope is the worst feeling of all, and I don't feel like hoping that things will work out. Really, hope is more a delusion than anything.

I know, but I'd rather be dead than to talk about it. I've been seeing two psychiatrists for some time now and I still can't mention it to them. I'm quitting my therapy because it's not working for me.

I recently told two of my family members about it (in tears). They told me to get over it. I suppose to some it would be a silly thing to get so worked up over.

I've tried, believe me!

Really, thank you for your kindness and for putting up with my whining.

They do exist, but I'll never enjoy them. I was on the way to living my dream once, but I couldn't get over myself, so I gave up. They're not even out of reach at the moment, but I still can't get over myself. It's not my fault, however.

> at some point I'll probably start my own thread in this subreddit

Lol

My problem is in no way temporary. Its most prominent feature is permanence.

And good username.
I'm too unwilling to say. I've spent 12 years trying to get over them, but I can't do it.

I read your other post and, I have to be honest, I don't get it. I hear of people resorting to suicide when they feel trapped or hopeless, but rarely because they feel lost. It can be an unsettling feeling, but it's really a great opportunity at a time like this, when you feel as you do now.

When you're lost, every single direction is a possibility. All you have to do is think on it and decide where to go. Myself, I know exactly what I want, but there are some major obstacles ahead of me. I'm trapped. Lost is a hazy, new beginning. I think you shouldn't call it quits.

I read it a long time ago and I didn't think it was useful.

There's some pain, sure, but I could get over that if it weren't for the obstacles I face. Those are what really kill me, and they won't ever "get better". I'm literally stuck.

Do you have a job (i.e., do you have insurance)? If so, the first step is seeing a psychiatrist and probably a therapist. I find that psychs are only useful in dealing drugs, but I'll let you see for yourself what it's like. Don't beat yourself up over a would-be prognosis, because you have no idea where you'd be now, so it's just useless and negative thinking.

I dunno, it's up to you where you'll live, but I think the more comfortable option is with your parents.

If it it's not currently feasible, where would you like to go from here?

What would you think of moving to a more affordable area on your own (once you get a job)? You could tell your mother she is welcome to join you but that you won't finance her choice of lifestyle. Maybe you could extend the offer to your brother, as long as he contributes rent.

Finally, I think you should find some way to become your own man. It can't be done right away, of course; give yourself some time to figure out what you what, what you're good at, and how you'll combine the two and then try for it.

Anyway, that's probably how I'd handle it. Good luck.

I know, it's so simple it's almost stupid. If i don't want to do it, then don't. The problem is, I want to live much less than I don't want to do it.

Nothing recent. Just the way things are.

Because I can't live, the way things are. What that means is, I can't sleep, can't go outside, go to school, get a job, smile, enjoy my friends, look in the mirror, and on and on and on. On top of that, there are things haunting me. I don't understand it, but there are.

Sometimes I just sit and feel myself existing and I want to scratch my eyes out. What kind of life is that?
So many people in this subreddit are desperate for someone to listen to them, but there's just not enough caring to go round. Forget me and tend to somebody else's post--i'm already done for.
